title: Henningkager (Honey Cakes)
description: A cake made with honey, syrup, and butter.

ingredients.name: 18 quintal potassium carbonate, dissolved in a cup of cold water
ingredients.sourceText: 18 quintal potassium carbonate, dissolved in a cup of cold water

steps: Give the syrup and honey a good boil. To this add the butter. Dissolve the potassium carbonate in a cup of cold water and measure out the flour in a dish. When the syrup has cooled enough that you can hold your hand in it, pour it onto the flour, add the dissolved potassium carbonate, and stir the whole together into a dough, which stands in a crock for 5-6 days in a cold place. Immediately before baking, a little spice can be added. The oven must be well heated. The whole is baked as one large cake of appropriate thickness, which is cut into oblong, square small cakes when it is taken from the oven. A scalded almond can be placed in the middle of each cake.

title: Hindbær-Eddike (Raspberry Vinegar)
description: Prepared with vinegar, berries, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: (1 pound) powdered sugar per liter of juice
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 kg (1 pound) powdered sugar per liter of juice

steps: Place the berries in a crock and cover with vinegar
Tie the crock well and let stand for 3 to 4 days in a cold place

Let the juice that runs through stand until the next day
Measure it and boil for 10 to 12 minutes with 1/2 kg powdered sugar per liter of juice
Skim carefully during cooking
Pour into bottles, cork and seal with plaster

title: Hindbær-Suppe (Raspberry Soup)
description: A soup made with raspberries, corn, and water.
steps: Pick, clean and place the raspberries over the fire in 3 pints water.

This boils as long as until all juice is extracted from the berries, then strain it through a fine sieve and place it over the fire again with sugar according to how sour the berries are; it may well be brown sugar.
Reserve a little of the soup after it is strained, and stir a large spoonful of corn-starch into it.
When the soup is near boiling, stir this in, it boils up again and is then ready to serve.
Serve with rusks.

title: Hindbærsaft (Raspberry Juice)
description: Prepared with raspberries and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: 2 to 3 pounds of powdered sugar per pot of juice
ingredients.sourceText: 2 to 3 pounds of powdered sugar per pot of juice

steps: Mash the berries in a pot and wring them in a clean linen cloth
Place the sugar in the juice to dissolve overnight

Fill it cold into bottles
Berries can be gathered over several days in a pot and should then be mashed gradually and stirred a couple of times daily
Otherwise treat as described above

title: Hominy-Vandgrød (Hominy Water Porridge)
description: Prepared with hominy, water, and salt.
steps: For ½ kg grains, use 2 L cold or lukewarm water; let them stand until the next day.
Pour everything into an enameled pot with approximately 2 L boiling water.
Cook the porridge for 1 hour over the heat and then place it in a hay box, where it stands for about 4 hours.
All grain types must be well cooked.
Salt the porridge and serve with butter, sugar and sweet milk.
Hominy is American corn grains, very nourishing and cheap.

title: Honse-Frikashee (Chicken Fricassee)
description: Prepared with hen, peppercorns, and carrot.
steps: Clean the hen and chop it up; first take off the legs and wings
Split the breast and back, and chop these into suitable pieces
Place over heat in boiling water that must come just over them
Skim as often as foam rises, then add a tablespoon of salt, a dozen peppercorns, a carrot, an onion, a couple of cloves, and a bunch or bouquet of dried vegetables
Cook gently until the hen is tender, about one hour, then remove it and keep it warm while the sauce is made
Strain the soup and return it without vegetables to heat; stir together a lump of butter and a lump of flour over the heat
Gradually stir in 0.5 pint of the soup, adding a beaten egg yolk and stirring until the sauce is smooth
Add salt and pepper, and serve on a warm dish

title: Hummer i Fiskerand (Lobster in Fish Border)
description: Prepared with fish, lobster, and wheat flour.

ingredients.name: Cooked Asparagus pieces one inch in length
ingredients.sourceText: Cooked Asparagus pieces one inch in length

steps: Fill a greased ring mold with fish forcemeat and place it in a pan with enough water to reach halfway up the mold.
Cover with a piece of paper greased with butter and cook for about a quarter hour.
Turn the mold onto a serving dish and let it stand for a few minutes before lifting off the fish border.
Prepare the lobster stewing: Pick the cooked lobster and cut the meat into small pieces.
Melt a piece of butter and stir in one tablespoon of wheat flour.
Add one pail of strong broth and one pail of cream, and cook together.
Pour this sauce over small cooked fish balls and lobster meat to warm it.
Add small pieces of cooked asparagus about one inch in length to the mixture.
Fill the fish border with the lobster mixture and serve as hot as possible.

title: Hummer-Suppe (Lobster Soup)
description: A soup made with lobsters, stock, and white pepper.
steps: Rinse the lobsters and place them in boiling water
When the legs come off easily, remove the lobsters
Cool them, split them open and remove the meat from the tail and claws in pieces as large as possible
Cut the meat into small, uniform pieces and place in a tureen
Pound all remaining parts of the lobsters - shells, bones and roe - in a mortar together with 175 gr butter
Pour this mixture into 4 L spare soup together with a good whisk and cook for 10 minutes so that the red lobster butter can collect on top
Skim off the red butter, then bake 100 gr flour in the soup and thin with the lobster soup
Add ground white pepper and Madeira
Add {{source-6}}, the lobster meat and small fish balls to the soup
Serve with Butter dough slices or Simels and add the asparagus water to the soup

title: Hvedebrod (Wheat Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with yeast, flour, and water.

ingredients.name: 0.5 gill yeast or 2 cents compressed yeast
ingredients.sourceText: 0.5 gill yeast or 2 cents compressed yeast

steps: Put {{source-0}} in a deep vessel
Make a hole in the center
Add 1 quart lukewarm water, {{source-2}}, {{source-3}}, and 0.5 gill yeast or 2 cents compressed yeast dissolved in a little lukewarm water
Have more lukewarm water ready and use as much as needed to make a fairly soft dough
Knead thoroughly with both hands; the softer the dough, the better the bread, as long as it releases from the hands and vessel
When even and good, sprinkle a little flour on it, lay a folded cloth over the vessel, and let it stand four or five hours in a warm place to rise
If the dough was stirred in the evening, it can stand overnight if the room is warm
When risen enough, turn out onto a floured breadboard and knead for about fifteen minutes, using enough flour so it does not stick to the board or hands
Put it back in the bread pan and let it rise fully again, which happens faster than the first time
Divide the dough into 4 breads, put in baking pans, let stand fifteen minutes, then bake in a hot oven
The recipe makes about 8 pounds of bread; divided into 4 pieces, bake for one hour
Test with a splint or straw; if it comes out clean, the bread is done
It should also have the proper color

title: Hvedebrød (Wheat Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with wheat flour, yeast, and milk.

ingredients.name: thick yeast (or 20 grams pressed yeast)
ingredients.sourceText: 2 tablespoons thick yeast (or 20 grams pressed yeast)

steps: Knead the wheat flour with the lukewarm milk, a little salt, and yeast until the dough releases from the hands.
Let it rise well covered for 3 or 4 hours.
If baking in the morning, the dough can be laid out in the evening and left overnight in cold water to rise in a moderately warm place.
Knead the dough again and shape into 3 or 4 loaves, which should rise a little more.
Brush with egg white, water, or beer and place in a well-heated oven that is not so hot that the crust burns.
Since the heat is strongest at the back of the oven, it may be right to turn the pan once during baking, which takes 1 hour.
If the loaves should be smooth, make one or two cuts lengthwise or crosswise; the deeper the cut, the thicker the crust becomes.
The crust will be thinner by beginning baking with slightly less heat; for this purpose, you can leave the oven door slightly ajar.
When the loaves are taken out, it is good to cover them slightly so the cooling proceeds more slowly.
The milk used can also be skimmed, but it must in no way be sour, nor must the yeast be bitter.

title: Hvid Fiskesauce (White Fish Sauce)
description: A sauce made with cornstarch, fish broth, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: A couple spoonfuls of Madeira or other wine
ingredients.sourceText: A couple spoonfuls of Madeira or other wine

steps: Knead cornstarch into a good piece of butter
Place this in a large cup of sieved strong fish broth and bring to a boil
Whip 2-3 egg yolks and stir into the sauce while it is removed from the heat
When it is about to boil again, add a couple spoonfuls of Madeira or other wine
Whip well until it is poured out
Add a little nutmeg and salt if needed

title: Hvid Havre-Suppe (White Oat Soup)
description: A soup made with groats, egg yolks, and egg white.
steps: Sprinkle the grains into the boiling water and cook ½ to 1 hour.
Strain the soup and pour into a serving bowl in which 2 egg yolks and 1 egg white have been stirred with approximately ¼ kg powdered sugar.
Into this thickened soup pour ¼ L good sherry and ¼ L rhubarb juice.
Whole cinnamon and lemon peel can be cooked in the soup or rather together with the grains.
This can be served with compote of fresh, dried or preserved fruit.

title: Hvid Sagosuppe (White Sago Soup)
description: A soup made with sago, raisins, and lemons.
steps: Pick and wash the raisins.

Beat 5 egg yolks with 5 spoonfuls of powdered sugar, then whisk this mixture into the soup.
Just before serving, add the lemon slices (with pits removed), sugar to taste, and half a bottle of old white wine.

title: Hvid Sauce (White Sauce)
description: A sauce made with bouillon, wheat flour, and meat.
steps: For 1 Quart Bouillon take 1 Tablespoon good Wheat Flour, which is stirred out in a piece of Butter.
This must first be melted in a Pot, and when it begins to boil, put the Flour in and rub it out.
It must absolutely not become brown, and it is gradually thinned with the Broth.
Add Nutmeg, Cayenne, white Roots, small Meat balls, and otherwise what you have of preserved Oysters, Capers or Anchovies.
If it is for Chickens, Turkeys or Calf's Breast, it is also good to whisk a Spoon of Cream into the Sauce when it is to be served; but for Geese and Ducks it does not suit.
Have the Sauce a little sharper with Cayenne for these, and do not use Oysters.
If you want to make the White Sauce for Geese sour and sweet, then do not make it so sharp, and use only white Roots and Apples.
Some use sliced Almonds and Currants for this.

title: Hvid Sauce til Høns, Kalve- og Lammekjød (White Sauce for Chicken, Veal and Lamb)
description: A sauce made with cream, lemon, and bouillon.

ingredients.name: Shell of half a small Lemon
ingredients.sourceText: Shell of half a small Lemon

steps: Boil 1 Pint Cream very gently with a little crushed Pepper, preferably white, and the Shell of half a small Lemon.
When it has boiled a little, add a Thickening of 2 to 3 Ounces Butter (depending on how thick the Cream is), stirred with {{source-4}}.
Stir constantly until it has become thick, and then thin it with Bouillon until the Sauce has obtained a suitable Thickness.
When serving, press the Juice of half a Lemon into it.
Good Milk may be used instead of Cream, but then use more Butter.
Instead of Lemon Shell and Juice, cook so much strong Broth or good Soy in the Sauce that it gets a reddish Colour.
For 8 to 10 Persons.

title: Hvid Soya af Agurker (White Soy from Cucumbers)
description: Prepared with seeds, vinegar, and salt.

ingredients.name: flesh, seeds and juice from hollowed cucumbers
ingredients.sourceText: flesh, seeds and juice from hollowed cucumbers

steps: Place the flesh, seeds and juice hollowed from cucumbers on the stove with a little salt and cook for 1/2 hour with constant stirring so nothing sticks, which would give a burnt or musty taste; if this happens the whole must be discarded
Press through a sieve
Return the juice to the stove with one gill vinegar per pint of juice and cook until it is smooth, about 1/2 hour
Place in small bottles or jars and bind well the next day
This soy gives a pleasant flavor in all kinds of white sauces, fricassees and the like, and must be added early so it cooks a bit with the sauce

title: Hvid Vin-Gelé (White Wine Jelly)
description: Prepared with powdered sugar, wine or madeira or sherry, and isinglass.

ingredients.name: 1 bottle Rhenish wine or Graves (with a little Madeira or Sherry optionally added)
ingredients.sourceText: 1 bottle Rhenish wine or Graves (with a little Madeira or Sherry optionally added)

steps: Cook the chopped powdered sugar with {{source-1}} to a syrup.
Pour in 1 bottle Rhenish wine or Graves, but the wine must not boil.
Melt 12 sheets of isinglass in 1 1/4 dl (1/2 pint) water without boiling and stir into the jelly.
Pour the jelly through a clean cloth into a mold moistened with water and strewn with sugar.
Fresh grapes can be layered in the mold: pour a little jelly into the bottom, and when it is set, lay some grapes, then jelly again and more grapes, until the mold is full.
While the mold is being filled, keep the remaining jelly near heat so it does not set.
The jelly can be arranged in small mounds on pineapple slices, decorated with grapes and foam peaks, and garnished with petits fours.
Prepared this way, it is not necessary to clarify the jelly.
At serving, turn the jelly out and serve with cream sauce.

title: Hvide Pølser (White Sausages)
description: Prepared with rice, melted butter, and raisins.
steps: 2 Pounds of scalded rice groats are cooked half-soft into a stiff porridge in 3 pots of sweet milk.

When the porridge is somewhat cooled, add 20 Quintals of melted butter, 10 beaten eggs, 0.5 Pound of washed raisins without seeds, 0.5 Pound of finely chopped lard, 12 Quintals of sweet and 5 Quintals of bitter, finely ground almonds, 18 Quintals of ground icing sugar and a little ground nutmeg.
Stir everything well and stuff into cleaned intestines that have first lain for one hour in soak in lukewarm milk.
They are then cooked in water with a little salt in it.
The sausages should not be stuffed too firmly; the intestines should only be three-quarters full.
They are arranged whole, either boiled or roasted with melted butter.

title: Hvidkaal (White Cabbage)
description: Prepared with cabbage, bouillon, and cream.
steps: Prepare like cauliflower, cut into 4 parts for cooking, and when they are to be stewed, cut them again into smaller pieces and keep warm while the sauce is made. A good piece of butter is stirred with a little nutmeg over heat and served in a sauce bowl or poured over the cabbage when it is arranged. You can also stir flour into melted butter, approximately 1 ounce flour in 2 ounces butter, spread it with bouillon and give the cabbage a brief cooking in this together with salt and nutmeg. You can stew the cabbage in milk, then melt a little butter, in which flour is stirred out, cream or milk, and it is cooked evenly. The cabbage then gets a brief cooking in this with a piece of sugar and finally salt. In everything where there is milk, salt is added last and only after it is taken off the heat.

title: Hvidkaal-Suppe (White Cabbage Soup)
description: A soup made with cabbage, stock, and peppercorns.
steps: Cooked mostly the same as green cabbage soup on salted pork.
Divide 1 head white cabbage into 4 parts, which are scalded in boiling water.
Cut away the stem and chop the cabbage finely.
A couple of spoonfuls of flour can be chopped into the cabbage as directed for green cabbage, or it can be baked as with other thickened soups.
Cook the cabbage for a quarter hour in the stock together with {{source-2}} and 20 peppercorns.
Peeled potatoes cooked in the stock can be served with it; the pork is served alongside.

description: A soup made with cabbage, pork or salt or meat, and carrots.

ingredients.name: Svineryg (pork back) or other pork or salt meat, 8 til 10 Pd.
ingredients.sourceText: Svineryg (pork back) or other pork or salt meat, 8 til 10 Pd.

ingredients.name: Et fast Hvidkaalshoved (a firm head of white cabbage)

ingredients.sourceText: Raaskrællede, kogte og ituskaarne Kartofler (raw peeled, cooked, and cut potatoes)

steps: Break the pork back at the joints before cooking.
Place 8 to 10 pounds of pork in a pot with enough water to cover it well.
Remove the outer leaves and tough stalk from the cabbage head; cut the rest into fine strips.
When the broth has boiled and been skimmed, add the cabbage strips along with carrots, parsley roots, and celery.
Place 20 whole peppercorns and a small tablespoon of ground caraway in a small tied linen bag and add to the soup.
Remove the bag before serving.
When the cabbage and vegetables are tender, remove them and cut the vegetables in pieces.
Strain the broth and bring to a boil again.
Pour into a tureen with the cabbage, vegetables, and raw peeled, cooked, and cut potatoes.
Sprinkle the pork back with a little salt and serve alongside the soup.

title: Hyben (Rose Hip Preserve)
description: A fruit preserve made with powdered sugar, vinegar, and rose water.
steps: Select beautiful large red garden rose hips that are firm in flesh and dry carefully with a cloth.
Keep the stems on but remove the sepals.
Cut a slit lengthwise into each fruit with a knife and remove the small seeds and hairs through the slit.
Boil sugar, rose water, and vinegar together to make a syrup and skim.
Add the fruit and boil until tender.
Pour everything through a sieve and boil the liquid again over heat until well reduced.
Mix the fruit with the syrup and pour into glasses or jars and tie them up when the preserve is done.
When serving, pour a little rose water over it for a fine effect.

title: Hyben med Rom (Rose Hip Preserve with Rum)
description: A fruit preserve made with rum, powdered sugar, and rose hips.
steps: Prepare the rose hips according to the previous instructions.
Place them in boiling water and boil until tender, then immediately strain through a sieve.
Melt the sugar in 1/4 liter of the water in which the rose hips were boiled and pour the warm syrup over them.
Over the next two days, drain the syrup and reboil it, pouring it over the fruit only after it has cooled.
On the fourth day, drain the syrup again and boil it down to a very thick syrup.
Add the rose hips without boiling them again.
After partially cooling, pour the rum over the preserve.
Pour into glasses and tie them up.

title: Hyldebærsaft (Elder Berry Syrup)
description: Prepared with berries and farina.

ingredients.name: 125 gr (1/4 lb) farina per 1 liter (1 pot) juice
ingredients.sourceText: 125 gr (1/4 lb) farina per 1 liter (1 pot) juice

steps: Pick the berries and put them in a pot; place over very low heat until they release their juice well, then strain through a fine sieve.
Measure the juice and boil for a quarter hour with the sugar; skim it and pour hot into bottles, which are tied immediately with parchment paper.

The elder berries are then boiled with water, with a little vinegar added, and the juice, after being strained, can be poured into dry bottles, corked, and gradually used in the household for elder berry soup.

description: Prepared with elderberries, powdered sugar, and cognac.

ingredients.name: powdered sugar per pot of juice
ingredients.sourceText: 3 pounds of powdered sugar per pot of juice

steps: Strip and place the berries over the fire, preferably in a clean earthenware pot
When they begin to burst, take them out, set them aside to cool and wring them in a clean linen cloth
Filter the juice if necessary and place it over the fire with the sugar and cinnamon
Cook with regular skimming until after about a quarter of an hour it begins to appear clear, then remove it from the fire and add a little Cognac
When the juice has cooled, fill it into bottles, whose upper part is filled again with Cognac
Cork the bottles well

Thicken the sauce with sago flour.
Pour the sauce over the chickens when serving and garnish with puff pastry strips or border.

title: Høns med Østers (Chicken with Oysters)
description: Prepared with oysters, chicken or capon, and lemon juice.
steps: Select an excellent, fat, and good chicken or capon. After cleaning and removing the skeleton, fill it with oysters and sew it closed along the back.
Place it on a rack in the pot to be steamed tender.
Boil the beard from the oysters in water with salt and lemon juice.
Mix it with a little stock made from the skeleton and neck, and add the oyster water from the shells.
Strain this stock and pour it over the chicken, which must not boil hard.
Within 1½ hours the meat will certainly be steamed tender, provided it is a young chicken.
For the sauce, make a beurre manié with flour and butter, dilute with the stock from the chicken, and bind with 2-3 egg yolks, seasoning with lemon juice and white wine.
Oysters can be added to the sauce, placing them in the hot sauce without bringing to a boil.
Remove the thread before serving the chicken.

title: Høns à la royale (Chicken à la Royale)
description: Prepared with chickens and calf sweetbreads.

ingredients.name: good, smooth ragout of calf sweetbreads and mushrooms
ingredients.sourceText: good, smooth ragout of calf sweetbreads and mushrooms

steps: Remove the skeleton from the chickens and fill them with a good, smooth ragout of calf sweetbreads and mushrooms.
Sew them closed tightly.
The chickens can either be boiled or roasted; if roasted, lard the breast with fine, fresh strips of fat.
For roasted chicken, make a brown mushroom sauce from the gravy. For boiled chicken, make a white mushroom sauce from the stock.
Serve the chickens with puff pastry strips or border.

title: Høns-Salat Nr. 1 (Chicken Salad No. 1)
description: A salad made with chicken, lettuce, and salad oil.

ingredients.name: Chicken, cooked until meat separates easily from bones
ingredients.sourceText: Chicken, cooked until meat separates easily from bones

ingredients.name: each of salt, dry mustard, and white pepper
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 teaspoon each of salt, dry mustard, and white pepper

steps: Cook chicken until meat separates easily from bones
Remove all meat from bones, free from skin and fat, and cut into pieces about 3/8 inch or smaller
Wash green lettuce, break into small pieces, and dry on a cloth
Mix meat and lettuce in a deep dish and season with {{source-2}}, {{source-3}}, and {{source-4}}
Prepare a mayonnaise as follows: blend 1 raw egg yolk with {{source-6}}, juice of 1/2 lemon, and cayenne pepper to taste
Mix well with a whisk, then add 3 gills salad oil and juice of 1/2 lemon drop by drop while stirring constantly
When two-thirds of the oil is incorporated, begin adding vinegar, totaling 4 tablespoons
Cover the salad with the mayonnaise and decorate with olives, capers, and hard-boiled eggs cut into quarters

description: A salad made with chicken, celery, and mustard.

ingredients.name: Chicken, cut into very small pieces
ingredients.sourceText: Chicken, cut into very small pieces

steps: Cut chicken meat from bones into very small pieces, almost like peas
Cut celery the same way
Use equal parts chicken and celery
Grind hard-boiled egg yolks finely; to each egg add 1/2 teaspoon mustard, same amount salt, 1 tablespoon oil, and 1 wine glass vinegar

Pour the sauce (to which a little cream has been added at the end) over them
Do not pour the sauce over until the salad is to be served

title: Hønse-Gelee (Chicken Jelly)
description: Prepared with chicken, water, and salt.

ingredients.name: salt and light seasoning, if the doctor permits
ingredients.sourceText: salt and light seasoning, if the doctor permits

steps: Pluck the chicken and remove all the fat; cut it open and clean carefully so as to avoid breaking the gall and entrails
Cut up the meat and break the bones into pieces
Place in a casserole with 2 quarts of cold water, bring slowly to a boil and skim until clear
Cover with a lid and simmer gently until the chicken has become a collapsed mass, about 2 to 4 hours
Strain through a flannel cloth until clear and return to the fire to boil gently until it has become a complete jelly
Test by placing a spoonful of jelly on a saucer; if it is stiff when cool, it is ready
Season lightly if the doctor permits and pour into cups; serve cold or slightly warmed

title: Hønse-Karry (Chicken Curry - East Indian Style)
description: Prepared with chickens, onions, and rice flour.

ingredients.name: dry curry or browned onions or chutney for garnish
ingredients.sourceText: dry curry or browned onions or chutney for garnish

steps: Brown a good slice of butter in a pot.
Sauté the chopped onions and curry in the butter.
Add the raw chickens cut into 4 to 6 pieces.
Pour in 1½ liters of boiling water and add salt.
Cook the chickens until tender.
Thicken the sauce with rice flour mixed in water and allow to boil well.
Serve with both mashed potatoes and rice.
Place the mashed potatoes in a mound in the center of a platter, arrange the chicken in curry around it, and place rice in a ring around the outside.
Sprinkle with dry curry or garnish with browned onions or chutney.

title: Hønsekjød-Suppe No. 2 (Chicken Soup No. 2)
description: A soup made with hen, vegetables, and beef.
steps: Cook a hen with white root vegetables and beef in so much water that it stands over it
When it is done, take it out and cut the meat from the bones in small pieces; the bones are cut up and cook somewhat longer in the soup
Strain this and place it back on the fire with the cooked white root vegetables and chicken meat to get a little boil
Then pour it into the tureen in which 4 egg yolks have been beaten
It is good to have 1/2 pint white wine and a little nutmeg in the eggs
Eaten with toasted bread

title: Hønsekjødsuppe (Chicken Soup)
description: A soup made with hen, vegetables, and bread.
steps: If you do not wish to use the cooked hen as a second course, this soup can be made with an old bird.
When the hen is slaughtered, soak it for one hour in cold water, then scald, pluck, clean and place it over heat with 3 pots water.
If you also have a veal shank to put in the pot, the soup will be much stronger.
When the soup boils, skim it well, add a little salt and soup vegetables, then continue cooking under even heat and under a covered lid until the vegetables are tender.
Remove these, cut them into pieces and place them in the tureen, while the soup continues to cook until the meat is tender.
Remove it, strain the soup and give it a good boil with the dumplings, and when the dumplings are tender, pour the soup into the tureen.
You can use small, fine dumplings or bread dumplings.
If the hen is old, it must preferably be chopped up before cooking, and all strength extracted from it, so the meat is not worth much.
Young hens (or turkeys) are instead cooked whole and can be served as a second course with cream horseradish.
To prevent the liver from cooking apart, place it during cooking inside the carcass with the cleaned giblets and heart.

title: Hønsekød-Suppe (Chicken Soup)
description: A soup made with hens, veal, and celery.
steps: Place the hens and veal shank in cold water with salt, equal in amount to the poultry.
Once the scum has been removed, add 1 celery, 4 carrots, and a good bunch of herbs.
Cook until the hens are tender.
Strain the soup through a fine sieve, leaving only a little liquid in the pot to keep the hens steaming hot until serving.
Skim the fat well from the soup, and only when it has been returned to the fire and comes to a boil again, pour it into the tureen.
Serve with small cut filets of meat, meatballs, vegetables, and similar garnishes.

This portion of batter is sufficient for 8 persons.

title: Indbagte Æbler i Butterdejg (Apples Baked in Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with apples, puff pastry, and fruits or strawberry or plum or prune.
steps: Peel the apples, remove the blossom and stem, and hollow out the core cavity so the apples remain whole.
Fill the cavity with various fruits such as a large preserved strawberry, plum, or prune (with the pit removed and a blanched almond inserted in its place), or leave empty.
Cover each apple completely with a thin layer of puff pastry, sealing it at the bottom near the stem, which should be turned downward on the baking sheet.
Brush the apples with beaten egg and sprinkle with a good layer of sugar.
Place on the baking sheet in a well-heated oven and bake for approximately 3/4 hour so the apples become very tender.
Serve very hot, placed on a napkin on a plate.
Whipped cream can be served separately.

title: Indisk Pickles (Indian Pickles)
description: Prepared with vinegar, mustard, and carrots.

ingredients.sourceText: A little Indian saffron to give it a suitable yellow color, or 2 tablespoons curry

ingredients.sourceText: String beans (ribboned and cut into smaller pieces)

ingredients.name: Pearl beans (ribboned and cut into smaller pieces)
ingredients.sourceText: Pearl beans (ribboned and cut into smaller pieces)

steps: Place the spices in a larger jar and pour the boiling vinegar over them.
Cover the jar and let it stand for the next day to be tied shut.
As the vegetables mentioned in the previous recipe appear during the course of the summer, rinse them in a little cold vinegar and dry them in a cloth before placing them in the jar.

For the cabbage, cut a medium-sized white cabbage head into strips and sprinkle this cabbage together with the chopped cauliflower with salt and let it stand in a dish for a couple of days; then pour off the brine and press the cabbage dry in a cloth before filling it into the jar.
When you have collected what you want for the pickles jar, pour off the vinegar and mix the vegetables together well as they are placed in smaller glasses or jars.

Give the vinegar a boil and pour it boiling over the vegetables in the glasses, which, as soon as the vinegar is cold, are tied shut either with bladders, parchment paper, or, in the case of the smaller glasses, corked and sealed.
There must be plenty of vinegar over the vegetables; if, after it has boiled, there is not enough, some more must be boiled, which is added spices in proportion to the amount of vinegar.
This pickles can keep for years, but must stand for 1 year before being used; otherwise the boiling of the vinegar must be repeated a couple of times to soften the vegetables.

title: Irsk Stuvning (Irish Stew)
description: Prepared with fat or butter or margarine, cabbage, and potatoes.

ingredients.name: meat (lamb breast, beef brisket, or lightly salted striped pork)
ingredients.sourceText: 1.5 kg meat (lamb breast, beef brisket, or lightly salted striped pork)

steps: On the bottom of a pot place a little fat, butter or margarine.
A fairly large cabbage head is cut very coarsely, and the bottom of the pot is covered with some of this cabbage.
Thereon is laid a layer of raw, peeled potatoes cut into 2-4 pieces.
1.5 kg meat is cut into smaller pieces; this can be either lamb breast, fat beef brisket or lightly salted striped pork cut into slices.
The meat is laid over the potatoes, sprinkled with ground pepper, and for fresh meat also with salt.
The meat is covered again with potatoes, and on top cabbage is laid.
Melted butter is poured over, the amount depending on the fattiness of the meat.
The lid is placed on the pot and must close well, since the dish must be softened by steam.
The pot, which must be shaken regularly during cooking, which lasts 3 hours, is placed over low heat to prevent the cabbage from burning on.
Meat and cabbage are arranged together on a dish.

title: Is-Punch à la Romaine (Punch Ice à la Romaine)
description: Prepared with powdered sugar, orange, and juice.

ingredients.name: Thinly pared and sliced zest of 1 orange
ingredients.sourceText: Thinly pared and sliced zest of 1 orange

ingredients.name: 1/4 bottle good aged rum or arrack
ingredients.sourceText: 1/4 bottle good aged rum or arrack

ingredients.name: Foam from 4 to 5 stiffly beaten egg whites
ingredients.sourceText: Foam from 4 to 5 stiffly beaten egg whites

ingredients.name: Or alternatively foam from 1/2 L (1/2 pot) cream
ingredients.sourceText: Or alternatively foam from 1/2 L (1/2 pot) cream

steps: Cook the powdered sugar with the water to a thin syrup.
When cold, add the thinly pared and sliced orange zest along with the juice of 2 oranges and 2 lemons.
After 15 minutes pass, strain the whole mixture and pour it into the freezing container.
Pack this in a mixture of finely chopped ice and Spanish salt; treat as otherwise done when freezing ice.
Into the frozen mass work in 1/4 bottle of good aged rum or arrack along with 1 bottle of white wine or champagne.
Sprinkle 100 gr powdered sugar into the foam of 4 to 5 stiffly beaten egg whites, stir with a light hand until well blended, and stir this egg white mixture into the punch shortly before serving.
Alternatively cream foam can be used instead of the egg white mixture.
Serve this thick punch preferably in flat champagne glasses; pour into glass decanters.

Suppen serveres med reven Parmesan Ost til.

title: Jordbær-Gelé (Strawberry Jelly)
description: Prepared with strawberries, powdered sugar, and isinglass.

ingredients.name: 10 sheets isinglass per liter (pot) of juice
ingredients.sourceText: 10 sheets isinglass per liter (pot) of juice

steps: Cook the strawberries, powdered sugar, and water together until the berries are cooked.
Pass them through a jelly bag or a dense cloth.
For each liter (pot) of juice, take 10 sheets of isinglass, dissolved in a little of the warm juice without allowing it to boil.
Stir it into the remaining juice, which is poured into a moistened and sugar-strewn ring mold.
Place on a cold spot or on ice until the next day.
At serving, turn the ring out onto a plate, and place a dollop of whipped cream in the center.
The jelly ring can be decorated around the outside with fresh, beautiful strawberries that have been standing for an hour, strewn with sugar.

title: Kaal-Dolma (Cabbage Dolma)
description: Prepared with cabbage, forcemeat, and broth or water.
steps: Separate the cabbage leaves and place them briefly in boiling water to soften and make them pliable
Remove the coarsest part of the stems from the leaves
Place a spoonful of forcemeat in each leaf
Roll the cabbage carefully around the forcemeat to form long rolls and bind with twine
Place the dolmas side by side in a pot with browned butter
When browned, pour a little broth or salted water over them
Cook under a closed lid for at least 2 hours
When tender, strain the gravy and thicken it into sauce with a nice brown color
Pour the sauce over the dolmas when serving

Alternative: use a Bavarian sausage instead of forcemeat, or place a cooked leek on a piece of white cabbage leaf, wrap the leaf around it, and place another leaf on top, then bind, brown, and cook as for cabbage dolma with forcemeat

title: Kalkun med Trøffel (Turkey with Truffles)
description: Prepared with turkey, truffles, and veal.
steps: Clean a young, fat turkey as usual and remove the innards.
Pat dry but do not wash.
Finely chop 4 pounds of veal meat from the leg with 3 pounds of kidney fat, 4 pounds of beef marrow, and a small glass of truffles, setting aside some of the largest truffle pieces.
Work the stuffing together with 3 eggs, salt, pepper, and a glass of good cognac.
While the turkey is still warm, fill the neck skin with the stuffing and sew it closed.
Fill the inside cavity with the remaining truffles and any leftover stuffing, being careful not to overfill as the stuffing will expand.
Let the turkey rest for a couple of days to absorb the truffle flavor.
Roast over gentle heat and arrange whole with truffle sauce.
Mushrooms may be substituted for truffles if desired.

title: Kalkunſteg (Roasted Turkey)
description: Prepared with turkey, bread, and water.
steps: Wash the turkey in cold water, then pour boiling water over it, let it lie for a couple of minutes and place it again in cold water.
If desired, you can stuff turkeys.
To fill the space where the crop has been, prepare a farce of several slices of wheat bread soaked in milk and then covered and left to stand for one hour.
Work a piece of cold butter until creamy, then stir in the bread after it has been crushed with a spoon, salt, a little ground ginger, a couple of cloves and three eggs.

When well mixed, you can add the crop, liver and heart, which are finely chopped, fill it in the skin and sew it, but the farce must not press down into the turkey, so a piece of wheat bread must be placed in the internal hole below the neck.
The oven must be well heated before the turkey is set in, and it must have an even heat, but not too strong, otherwise it will become too dark brown.
It cannot be roasted in a pot when it is stuffed.
Set it in with water and a little salt, with which it is gradually basted; later butter is placed on it, with which it is then basted.
A turkey requires two to three hours of roasting according to its size.

title: Kalkunſteg à l'Anglaise (Turkey Roasted in the English Manner)
description: Prepared with turkey, breadcrumbs, and egg white.

ingredients.name: One turkey, slaughtered a couple of days before use
ingredients.sourceText: One turkey, slaughtered a couple of days before use

steps: Slaughter a couple of days before use and hang it up by the legs.
Prepare in the usual manner.
Fill with finely grated breadcrumbs that are soaked with butter and two eggs and seasoned with salt, pepper, parsley, sage and marjoram.
Sew it up and roast in a roasting pan, preferably on a rack in the same; drip constantly with butter, pepper, salt and water and turn it.
A couple of minutes before it is done, glaze it with the white of an egg.
Take it out.

Most of the fat is poured off, and into it are put the chopped giblets with the water in which they were cooked, which is thickened with flour rubbed with butter; everything is stirred in the roasting pan and is given a good boil before it is served.
Gooseberry sauce is served with it.

title: Kallun-Suppe (Lamb Tripe Soup)
description: A soup made with lamb, peas, and butter or margarine.

ingredients.name: (20 skein) butter or vegetable margarine
ingredients.sourceText: 100 g (20 skein) butter or vegetable margarine

steps: Kallun soup is a summer dish which requires fresh vegetables to achieve the right flavor.
Cleaning tripe is work that must be done with great care and requires considerable time.
Split the bones before putting them in salted water.
Scrape the tripe at least 3-4 times, pouring boiling water over it in between.
Scrape and clean the fat intestines on the outside, then split and clean inside.
Cut these together with the tripe into small, square pieces.
Place the bones and cut tripe and fat intestines in a pot in 6 L (6 pots) salted water.

When the soup boils, skim well before adding vegetables, then simmer gently for about 3 hours under a closed lid or until the tripe is nearly tender; then add the shelled peas and about 20 cut new carrots and cook until tender.
In a pot, bake {{source-4}} and {{source-5}} and thin with some of the soup until it becomes a thick liaison, which is poured into the tripe soup.
Season with salt and ground pepper.

description: A soup made with tripe, vegetables, and carrots.

ingredients.name: Kallun, Fedetarme og Fødder af 5 Lam (tripe, mesentery, and feet from 5 lambs)
ingredients.sourceText: Kallun, Fedetarme og Fødder af 5 Lam (tripe, mesentery, and feet from 5 lambs)

ingredients.sourceText: Et godt Fjerdingspund Ris (a good quarter pound of rice)

steps: Clean the tripe, mesentery, and feet from 5 lambs with great care.
Scrape the tripe several times, placing it in cold salted water between each scraping.
Clean the mesentery first on the outside, then cut it open and clean the inside.
When the feet are cleaned, split the bones.
Cut the tripe into small cubes and place with the feet in 5 to 6 pots of water.
Bring to a boil and skim; add the mesentery (also cut into small cubes), salt, and a bunch of herbs.
Cook until the tripe is tender.
Add small soup vegetables, especially carrots, shelled peas, and rinsed raisins, along with rice prepared as described in recipe No. 6.
When the vegetables are tender, serve as hot as possible with finely chopped parsley.

title: Kalve i Karri (Veal Curry)
description: Prepared with veal or meat, onion, and wheat flour.

ingredients.name: Veal breast or other meat-rich cuts
ingredients.sourceText: Veal breast or other meat-rich cuts

steps: Chop the meat into small pieces and wash it in several changes of water.
Melt a large spoonful of butter in a pot over heat; when melted but not browned, add a small grated onion and cook for a couple of minutes.
Stir in two large spoonfuls of wheat flour and curry powder to taste, along with salt (use sparingly, about half a teaspoon, as more can be added later).
Cook this together and gradually add boiling water until it becomes a thick sauce.
Add the meat and gradually add more boiling water as needed, keeping the sauce fairly thick.
Cook covered as much as possible, but skim thoroughly.
The dish is ready when the meat is tender, which takes about an hour for a couple of pounds of meat.
Serve immediately with rice; if the sauce has become lumpy, remove the meat first and pour the sauce over it.

title: Kalve-Fricandeau (Veal Fricandeau)
description: Prepared with veal, stock or cream, and salt.
steps: Cut the inner loin into smaller pieces and beat lightly with a meat mallet and lard it. Sprinkle with salt and pepper, place with the larded side down against the pan, and fry in brown butter.
Within about 10 minutes they are as a rule fried. The gravy that has stuck to the pan is boiled off with stock or cream until it becomes smooth.
The sauce can also be made from butter and flour, which is thinned with the gravy. Serve with currant jelly, compote, salad, or vegetables.

Alternatively: prepare beforehand a sauce of butter and flour, browned well, thin this with stock, gravy, or boiling water and Maggi bouillon cubes, add coloring, and let the meat, previously browned, simmer in it. Before serving, some mushrooms are given a boil in the sauce; this is prepared with salt, sugar (very slightly) and wine.

title: Kalve-Frikassé (Veal Fricassée)
description: Prepared with veal or brisket, peppercorns, and onions.
steps: Use breast or brisket, chop into smaller pieces, rinse well and set to cook with cold water and a little salt and a bouquet garni.
When it boils, skim the soup several times; add some peppercorns and a couple of onions.
When the meat is cooked, remove it and strain the soup and reduce it with root vegetables and thicken with a tablespoon of flour mixed with butter until the thickness is appropriate.
Place the meat in the soup and warm it.
If you have asparagus, you can add cooked pieces about two inches long to the fricassée along with a little of the water in which they were cooked.

steps: Cut good veal into small pieces, beat them lightly, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and brown on both sides in approximately 8 to 10 minutes.

Just before serving add a piece of cold butter and a tablespoon of chopped parsley. Pour the sauce over the meat.
Serve with potatoes. Kallops can be made from pork tenderloin.

title: Kalvehjerte (Calf Heart)
description: Prepared with fat, coloring, and bouillon.

ingredients.name: One large, fat calf heart (serves 2-3 people)
ingredients.sourceText: One large, fat calf heart (serves 2-3 people)

steps: Open the heart by cutting it lengthwise and remove the blood vessels and tendons, then wash it thoroughly.
Stuff the heart like a chicken with parsley and butter.
Sew the heart together, brown it in butter, and add a little water along with coloring and salt.
Roast for about 3 hours.
Brown butter and flour together, then thin with the cooking liquid to make a sauce.
Strengthen the sauce with Maggi bouillon cubes if needed.
Cut the heart in half and cover with the sauce.
Serve with compote, currant jelly, salad, or browned potatoes.

title: Kalvehoved à la Maître d'Hôtel (Calf's Head in Maître d'Hôtel Style)
description: Prepared with calf's head, bouillon, and mushrooms.
steps: After the calf's head has been soaked, cleaned and cooked in very little water with salt and good bouillon, remove it from the bones and cut it into cubes when it is cold.
Brown butter and flour together and dilute with the bouillon to make a good, white, smooth sauce, and if necessary add Maggi Bouillon cubes.
Add mushrooms, white pepper, salt and a little sugar to the sauce, and lastly add the meat to warm it.
Just before serving, thicken the sauce with 3 to 4 egg yolks.
Serve in a puff pastry border or with slices and sprinkle with finely chopped parsley.

steps: Put a large tablespoon of butter over the heat in a pot; when it begins to brown, add two pounds veal, which can be simple meat, shoulder or neck, and brown it

It is an inexpensive and well-flavored dish

title: Kalvelever stegt som Bøf (Calf Liver Fried as Steak)
description: Prepared with calf liver, onion, and stock or broth or water.
steps: After the liver is drained and the membrane removed, cut it into very thin slices.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper, dip in flour, and fry on a pan in browned butter or Palmin.
In a good portion of butter, brown slices of onion and bake a spoonful of flour in it.

Once the sauce has boiled, pour it over the liver.
Serve with boiled potatoes.
Many people fry slices of salt pork alongside the liver, which improves the flavor of both. Serve both together in the sauce.

title: Kalvesteg (Veal Roast)
description: Prepared with veal and water.
steps: The veal leg is used for this roast. A typical weight for a leg is about 10 kg, and it can be roasted whole or divided.
The piece with the shank is the most advantageous, as it includes the large, tender piece of meat that is excellent both for the main course and later for use as cold cuts.
Veal can be stored for a few days in buttermilk or skim milk, which must be renewed every day or every other day, though it is best to prepare it without this preservation method.
When ready to use, rinse the meat well, pour boiling water over it, remove the skins, and lard it.

title: Karamel-Budding (Caramel Pudding)
description: A pudding made with icing sugar, egg yolks, and cream.
steps: Make the caramel the day before: cook {{source-0}} with 1 1/4 Dl (1/2 Pægl) water until dry, stirring constantly until it becomes liquid again and a beautiful brown color (do not let it become too dark or it will taste burnt)
Pour some of the caramel sugar into the dry mold and turn it well until a layer of sugar has set on both the sides and bottom
For the pudding: stir 12 egg yolks with 75 Gr (15 Kvint) icing sugar and whisk well with a whisk while stirring {{source-4}} into the mixture and adding vanilla essence
Stir regularly in the custard until it is cold, then fold in 6 whipped egg whites
Pour the pudding into the prepared mold and cook for approximately 2 hours until completely set
Keep the pudding in the mold until the next day
Serve on a not too flat platter with the caramel that comes with the pudding
For the remaining caramel sugar: dilute with water and stir with a little cream foam and a glass of cognac the next day, then serve with the pudding

title: Karamel-Creme (Caramel Cream)
description: A confection made with cream, powdered sugar, and skimmed milk.

Decorate with whipped cream mixed with vanilla extract

title: Karamelbudding (Caramel Pudding)
description: A pudding made with cream, egg yolks, and egg whites.
steps: Heat 1 pot sweet cream.
Whip together 10 egg yolks and 6 egg whites with 15 quintals finely ground melis sugar.
When the cream is hot, remove from heat and add the eggs while stirring constantly.
In a separate pan, dip 1 quarter-pound white sugar in water and bring to a boil until it becomes dry and again liquid.
Pour this caramel into a mold, turning and tilting it to coat all sides, ensuring no dry spots remain.
If any caramel remains, pour it into the cream.
Pour the cream into the caramel-lined mold, place the mold in water, and boil for one hour.
Prepare this pudding the day before, turn it out of the mold onto a dish, and serve cold.

title: Karotter (Pickled Carrots)
description: Prepared with carrots, white pepper, and vinegar.
steps: Scrape the small carrots, rinse them, and half-cook them in water.
Drain them in a colander and rinse them with cold water.
Dry the roots in a cloth and place them in glasses or jars together with the spices, which consist of some whole white pepper and a few Spanish pepper husks.
Pour over as much good pickling vinegar as is necessary to cover the vegetables.
Let them stand until the next day, then pour off the vinegar, give it a boil, and immediately pour it over the roots, after which the jar is tied shut with parchment paper.
Carrots can be peeled with a fluted herb knife and thereby get a beautiful appearance.

title: Kartoffel-Rouletter (Potato Roulettes)
description: Prepared with potatoes, cream, and bread crumbs.
steps: Grate cooked cold potatoes and mix with 2 eggs, 4 spoonfuls butter, a little sweet cream, salt, and pepper. Mix well together, and form the mixture into oblong or round roulettes, which are rolled in fine sifted bread crumbs and set aside for half an hour. Then dip them in egg whites and roll in bread crumbs, and thus they are breaded twice. Fry them in clarified butter, 5 to 6 pieces at a time, until they become beautifully golden brown. Take them out with a slotted spoon and place on a sieve so the butter can drip off. Use them as garnish for roasted meat and similar dishes.

title: Kartoffel-Sne (Potato Snow)
description: Prepared with potatoes, salt, and water.
steps: Boil very large, floury potatoes in salted water. As soon as they are tender, drain the water and keep the pot warm while peeling the potatoes and then pressing them through a purée sieve or grating over a very hot serving dish. Serve the potato snow as quickly as possible, and it must not be touched after it has been pressed through the sieve or grated on the grater, as handling it will cause it to lose its light appearance. Serve with spiced meat dishes such as breaded meat, goulash, boneless birds, etc.

Mix 18 drams potato flour with 1 measure thin cream and bake with the first mixture in the same way as making buns, until the dough leaves the pan

Serve warm, sprinkled with powdered sugar with a napkin around the dish

title: Kartofler (Potatoes)
description: Prepared with potatoes, water, and salt.
steps: Place them on the heat in as much water as it stands over them, salt is added and they cook continuously until they are tender, then drain the water, salt is sprinkled on and the pot is shaken well so the salt gets around, thereafter place the pot for half a dozen minutes at the back of the oven without a lid, so they can steam off and become dry. It is best that they are thereafter eaten immediately, but if you are obliged to wait, then as they are peeled, they can be placed in hot water with plenty of salt in; they are covered and placed at the back of the oven and in this way they can be kept good for a couple of hours. If they are very large potatoes, then you can peel them raw and either cook them whole or cut them in half; as you peel them they must be placed in cold water so they do not become dark. They are cooked and dried off like the previous ones.

title: Kastanier (Preserved Chestnuts)
description: Prepared with chestnuts, powdered sugar, and lemon juice.
steps: Remove the brown shell from large selected genuine chestnuts.
Place them for a few minutes in boiling water and then in cold water so that the inner thin seed coat can be removed more easily.
Place the peeled chestnuts in boiling water with lemon juice and boil until almost tender.
Remove them with a slotted spoon or place on a sieve.
Melt 1/2 kg sugar in 1 1/4 dl of the water in which the chestnuts were boiled and add lemon juice to taste.
Bring the chestnuts to a boil in this syrup and immediately pour into a jar and set aside until the next day.
The next day, drain the syrup, bring to a boil and pour boiling over the chestnuts.
On the third day, place the syrup back on the heat to reduce until smooth.
Add the chestnuts to the boiling syrup and pour into jars and tie them up while the preserve is still hot.

title: Kathrine-Blommekage (Katherine Plum Cake)

Knead together 3 eggs, 65 quintals flour, half pound sugar, and 12 quintals butter into a dough.
Roll the dough thin and line a pan with a removable bottom so the pan is completely covered.
Dry the dough either in a tart pan or in an oven where something has just been baked.
Whisk 12 egg yolks well together with half a pound powdered icing sugar.

Lay the plums on the dough in the lined form and pour the mixture over them.
Bake the cake in a tart pan with heat from above and much heat from below for one hour.
When serving, cover with whipped cream mixed with vanilla sugar.
The cake will sink somewhat in the center.

title: Kirsebær-Suppe (Cherry Soup)
description: A soup made with cherries, bread, and water.
steps: Pit and cook the cherries with 1 quart water, strain, cook again with 1 pint and pour into the first cooked soup.
To make the soup clear, lay a thin cloth in the sieve and pour the soup through it, after which place it on the fire with whole cinnamon, cloves and sugar to bring to a good boil.
Serve with bread dumplings, which are added when the soup boils, or with baked bread.
A few of the berries can be removed and cooked in the strained soup.
If you want the soup smooth, stir a heaping spoonful of corn-starch dissolved in water or in some of the soup while cold, diluted with the hot and stirred in when the soup boils.
The starch must only boil a few minutes to not become stringy.

title: Kirsebærsuppe (Cherry Soup)
description: A soup made with cherries, lemon, and potato flour.
steps: From 2 pounds of black preserved cherries, select a plateful of the best ones.
Crush the remainder so that the pits break apart; use more or fewer pits according to how much you want the kernel flavor to come through.
Put them over the fire with 3.5 pots of water, or enough so the water just covers the berries, and cook them until all the strength is extracted, which will take about a quarter hour.

Strain them, and put the strained soup back over the fire together with the cherries set aside the first time, several sticks of cinnamon, a couple of lemon slices without pits, and a little clove, and cook it; then thicken it with a little potato flour and top with small bread balls.
Before serving, sweeten to taste with sugar.
Alternatively, instead of bread balls, you can serve it with small rusks or baked wheat bread cubes.
Dried cherries can also be used for this soup.

ingredients.name: a small piece of candy sugar
ingredients.sourceText: a small piece of candy sugar

steps: For 10 pounds of soup meat, take 4 pounds of simpler beef, such as shank; after washing, chop it into pieces and place it over heat with 12 pots of cold water.
When this soup has been brought to boil over slow heat, skim it, and add a little salt, then boil the soup evenly for one hour.

Only then add the proper soup meat together with a soup bunch and some cleaned whole soup vegetables, 10 whole peppercorns and a small piece of ginger, then cook the soup evenly again until the vegetables are tender.
Remove these vegetables, cut them up and place them in the tureen.
When the meat is tender, remove it and keep it warm until serving.
Strain the soup and let it rest quietly for a quarter hour, then skim off the fat.
Now pour the soup carefully back into the pot so that no sediment comes with it.
Add a small piece of candy to the soup and, if necessary, salt it.
Add the dumplings, give it a good boil, and when the dumplings are tender, pour it into the tureen over the vegetables.
The portions mentioned here will be sufficient for 12 persons.
The soup meat is sprinkled with a little salt and can be served as a second course with horseradish sauce.
If soup is left over, the vegetables must be strained out, as it will easily turn sour during storage.

title: Kjørvelsuppe (Chervil Soup)
description: A soup made with chervil, bouillon or beef or lamb or broth, and asparagus.

ingredients.name: Nogle smaa kogte Gulerødder (small cooked carrots)
ingredients.sourceText: Nogle smaa kogte Gulerødder (small cooked carrots)

ingredients.name: Ristede Skiver af Franskbrød (toasted French bread slices)
ingredients.sourceText: Ristede Skiver af Franskbrød (toasted French bread slices)

steps: Rinse and finely chop 3 to 4 handfuls of chervil.
Heat 5 pots of bouillon (made from veal or lamb meat) and skim it.
Melt a quarter pound of butter in a saucepan and brown it for about a quarter hour.
Gradually thin the roux with the bouillon.
Cut cleaned asparagus into one-inch pieces, boil in water, and add to the soup along with some of the cooking water.
Add small cooked carrots and the chopped chervil to the soup.
Bring the soup to a boil and serve with poached eggs and toasted slices of French bread.

title: Klap Torske-Suppe (Clear Cod Soup)
description: A soup made with fish broth, meat, and carrots.
steps: Mix the broths together and cook with 4 to 5 carrots, 1 celery, 4 leeks and a good bunch.
When the vegetables are tender, remove them, cut them up and add them to the tureen, over which the broth is poured.
Finely chopped parsley can be added to this.
